Mask small numerators for sensitive data privacy

Source: R/get_masked.R
get_masked.Rd

Masks small numerators (counts) to protect patient privacy when the corresponding denominator (the total) is also shown. It applies two rules: (1) mask any numerator in the range (0, threshold), optionally together with zeros and NAs, and (2) make sure at least two values are masked, at least one of them positive, by also masking the next smallest positive value(s) if needed.

Rule 2 is the reason this function exists. If a denominator is published, a single masked numerator can be recovered by subtracting the visible numerators from the total. Masking at least two values, one of them positive, leaves the individual values undetermined. If the denominator is not shown, a simple ifelse() on the threshold should suffice and there's no need to use this function.

Usage

get_masked(
  vec,
  threshold,
  mask_label = "masked",
  mask_zero = FALSE,
  mask_na = FALSE
)

Arguments

vec

A numeric vector of count data (numerators) to be masked. Only values >= 0 and NA are accepted; negative values and non-numeric input throw an error. Note that a mixed vector such as c(1, 2, TRUE, FALSE) is coerced to numeric by R before reaching the function, so it will be silently allowed.

threshold

Numeric. The threshold value for masking. Values greater than 0 and less than threshold will be masked. As an example, the NPDA usually uses 3.

mask_label

Character string. The message to replace masked values with. Default is "masked".

mask_zero

Logical. If TRUE, zeros are masked as well. Default is FALSE, because a zero conveys a meaningful and positive message (e.g. no patients at this hospital has the disease) and does not put privacy at risk.

mask_na

Logical. If TRUE, NAs are masked as well. Default is FALSE, because an NA conveys a meaningful message (e.g. the hospital has unknown number of patients with the disease) and does not put privacy at risk.

Value

A character vector with masked values replaced by mask_label. If no values need masking, returns the original vector converted to character. Unmasked NAs are returned as NA_character_.

Details

The function implements a two-step masking process:

  1. Initial masking: Any values in the range (0, threshold) are masked, plus zeros if mask_zero = TRUE and NAs if mask_na = TRUE.

  2. Secondary masking: If anything was masked but fewer than two values were, or none of them is positive, the smallest unmasked positive value(s) are also masked, all occurrences at a time, until at least two values are masked and at least one is positive (or none are left).

Masked zeros and NAs: When mask_zero and mask_na are TRUE, zeros and NAs count towards the minimum of two masked values but cannot be the only ones. They add nothing to the total, so if only they were masked, subtracting the visible numerators from the denominator would reveal that every masked value is 0 or unknown, which is why the smallest positive value(s) must also be masked.

Note

The function always returns a character vector to facilitate merging with other masked datasets that may contain non-numeric mask messages.

Examples

# Positive values less than the threshold and the second smallest positive value are masked
vec1 <- c(5, 6, 4, 5, 1, 0, 0, NA)
get_masked(vec1, threshold = 3)
#> [1] "5"      "6"      "masked" "5"      "masked" "0"      "0"      NA      

# Custom mask message
get_masked(vec1, threshold = 3, mask_label = "*")
#> [1] "5" "6" "*" "5" "*" "0" "0" NA 

# No masking if all positive values are above the threshold
vec2 <- c(5, 6, 4, 5, 3, 0, 0, NA)
get_masked(vec2, mask_label = "*", threshold = 3)
#> [1] "5" "6" "4" "5" "3" "0" "0" NA 

# Custom threshold
get_masked(vec2, mask_label = "*", threshold = 4)
#> [1] "5" "6" "*" "5" "*" "0" "0" NA 

# Zeros are kept by default; mask_zero = TRUE masks them and the smallest positive values too
get_masked(vec1, threshold = 3, mask_label = "*", mask_zero = TRUE)
#> [1] "5" "6" "4" "5" "*" "*" "*" NA 

# NAs are kept by default; mask_na = TRUE masks them and the smallest positive values too
get_masked(vec1, threshold = 3, mask_label = "*", mask_na = TRUE)
#> [1] "5" "6" "4" "5" "*" "0" "0" "*"
get_masked(vec1, threshold = 3, mask_label = "*", mask_zero = TRUE, mask_na = TRUE)
#> [1] "5" "6" "4" "5" "*" "*" "*" "*"

# Realistic workflow example
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)

# Create example demographic data
set.seed(1234)
dat <- tibble(
  hospital_id = sample(8, size = 100, replace = TRUE),
  condition = sample(c("adhd", "asd", "dyslexia","prefer not to say"),
                     size = 100, replace = TRUE)
)
# Apply masking to grouped counts
results <- dat |>
  group_by(hospital_id, condition) |>
  summarise(numerator = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(
    denomiantor = sum(numerator),
    percent = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * numerator / denomiantor),
    numerator_masked = get_masked(numerator, threshold = 3, mask_label = '*'),
    percent_masked = ifelse(numerator_masked == '*', '*', percent)
  )
} # }
